newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RAUL GRABS CENTER-STAGE AS 'OLD FIRM' BREAKS CLEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAUL GRABS CENTER-STAGE AS 'OLD FIRM' BREAKS CLEAR.

text.p: Teenager Raul Gonzalez is set to sign a new multi-billion peseta contract with Real Madrid after taking centre-stage in one of the most exciting weekends of league action the Spanish league has seen in recent years.

The Raul-inspired 4-1 win at neighbours Atletico, together with Barcelona's victory at Real Betis, have left the 'old firm' pair four points clear of a fast-fading chasing group and increasingly likely to take Spain's two Champions' League places.
It could have been a very different story but for Raul.
The 19-year old kept his head to equalise just after the break and carried his side after striker Predrag Mijatovic was given a red card for insulting a linesman.
And in a memorable final ten minutes Raul did enough to make any Atletico fan weep.
Raul only left the club after club president Jesus Gil scrapped Atletico's junior sides as a cost-cutting measure.
Gil must have been ruing his decision as Raul picked up a ball outside the area and wriggled his way through the Atletico defence before scoring from a seemingly-impossible angle.
Moments later he set up Clarence Seedorf for the third, before rounding off a superb performance on the stroke of full-time by laying on the fourth for Victor Sanchez.
"It was unforgettable, a dream come true," said Raul.

Real chairman Lorenzo Sanz, whose first job on taking over at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium in November 1995 was to renegotiate Raul's contract, now wants to ensure his star isn't tempted by other teams.
Sanz is expected to raise Raul's salary, and with it the amount that must be paid to buy him from 1.6 billion pesetas ($12.2 million) to five billion pesetas ($38.2 million).
Even at that price, Sanz thinks that Raul -- who shot to prominence aged just 17 by scoring against Atletico on his home debut -- would be undervalued.
"He's worth 20 or 30 billion pesetas ($152 million to $229 million)," commented Sanz.
Many Spanish fans now rate him even more highly than the only other player in the league to command such astronomical figures.
A total of 85 per cent of callers in a phone-in organised by a regional television station said they thought Raul was better than Barcelona's Brazilian prodigy, Ronaldo.
Ronaldo scored another brilliant goal as Barcelona came back from 2-0 down to win 4-2 at high-flying Betis.

But on a day when players were meeting to discuss how to combat the influx of foreigners into the Spanish game it was ironic that the only other player to compete with Raul in Monday's headlines was another home-grown product.

Luis Enrique Martinez orchestated Barcelona's sensational come-back with a hat-trick of headers in the 4-2 win at Betis. His performance was so good that one newspaper looking for superlatives was forced to compare him with Raul.
